## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the Night of Power, on the sending down of the Quran in the month, and on the date of the night, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
- The chapters rest on separate passages. The verses do not say in so many words that the blessed night, the Night of Power and the month are one event; the inventory groups them, and a scholar should decide how the page states the link.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the date of the Night of Power and the identification of the Spirit named in the passage.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The Night of Power  (`#the-night-of-power`)

Cited ayat: 97:1-5

> **97:1** بِّسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ
>
> **97:2** وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ
>
> **97:3** لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
>
> **97:4** تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ
>
> **97:5** سَلَٰمٌ هِىَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ

### Claims

**c1** (97:1): God says that He sent it down in the Night of Power; the verse does not name what 'it' is.

**c2** (97:2): The verse asks the one addressed what would let him know what the Night of Power is.

**c3** (97:3): The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.

**c4** (97:4): The angels and the Spirit come down in it, by the permission of their Lord, with every matter.

**c5** (97:5): It is peace until the rising of dawn.

### One-minute summary

God says that He sent it down in the Night of Power [c1]. The Night of Power is better than a thousand months [c3], and the angels and the Spirit come down in it by the permission of their Lord [c4]. It is peace until the rising of dawn [c5].

### Complete story

God says that He sent it down in the Night of Power; the verse does not name what it is [c1]. The verse then asks the one addressed what would let him know what the Night of Power is [c2].

The Night of Power is better than a thousand months [c3]. The angels and the Spirit come down in it, by the permission of their Lord, with every matter [c4]. It is peace until the rising of dawn [c5].

### Deep study

The passage answers its own question by saying what the night is better than [c2][c3]. It speaks of a coming down of the angels and the Spirit, and says that it happens by the permission of their Lord [c4]. The last verse describes the night as peace and gives its end as the rising of dawn [c5].

### Kids mode

God says that He sent it down in the Night of Power [c1]. This night is better than a thousand months [c3]. The angels and the Spirit come down in it, by the permission of their Lord [c4]. It is peace until the dawn rises [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage invites attention to a single night by saying what it is better than [c3]. Another is that peace is how the passage describes the night [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which night this is, in which month, or how a believer would know it. The verses give none of this.
- Not established: what the thousand months measures, or how a night can be better than that; the verse says only that it is.
- Not established: what 'it' refers to in 97:1. Other chapters of this story speak of the Quran being sent down, and the inventory groups them; this verse does not name it.
- Not established: what 'every matter' includes, or who the Spirit is; the verse names the Spirit beside the angels and says no more here.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the date of the night and the identification of the Spirit. Neither is used in the story texts.

## 2. A blessed night  (`#the-blessed-night`)

Cited ayat: 44:2-6

> **44:2** وَٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
>
> **44:3** إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَٰرَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ
>
> **44:4** فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ
>
> **44:5** أَمْرًا مِّنْ عِندِنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ
>
> **44:6** رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

### Claims

**c1** (44:2-3): God swears by the clear Book and says that He sent it down in a blessed night.

**c2** (44:3): God says that He has always been one who warns.

**c3** (44:4-5): In that night every wise matter is made distinct, as a command from God, who says that He has always been one who sends.

**c4** (44:6): It is a mercy from the Lord of the one addressed, who is the one who hears and knows.

### One-minute summary

God swears by the clear Book and says that He sent it down in a blessed night [c1]. In it every wise matter is made distinct, as a command from Him [c3]. It is a mercy from the Lord of the one addressed [c4].

### Complete story

God swears by the clear Book and says that He sent it down in a blessed night [c1]. He says that He has always been one who warns [c2].

In that night every wise matter is made distinct, as a command from God, who says that He has always been one who sends [c3]. It is a mercy from the Lord of the one addressed, who is the one who hears and knows [c4].

### Deep study

The night is called blessed [c1], and the passage says that in it every wise matter is made distinct [c3]. The passage ties the sending down to warning [c1][c2] and to a command from God [c3]. It ends by naming the whole as mercy [c4].

### Kids mode

God says that He sent it down in a blessed night [c1]. God says that He has always been one who warns [c2]. It is a mercy from our Lord, who hears and knows [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage presents the sending down of the Book as warning and as mercy together [c2][c4]. Another is that it speaks of a night as blessed without describing what happens to it [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: that the blessed night here is the night of power of the previous chapter. The verses do not say so; the inventory and later readers group them.
- Not established: what the letters at the opening of the surah mean, or what 'made distinct' covers.
- Not established: what 'it' is in 44:3 beyond the clear Book that God swears by; whether it is the whole Quran or a part is not said.
- Not established: when the blessed night was or in what month.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of this night with the night of power. It is not used in the story texts.

## 3. The month of the sending down  (`#the-month`)

Cited ayat: 2:185

> **2:185** شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٍ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ وَلِتُكْمِلُوا۟ ٱلْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:185): The month of Ramadan is the one in which the Quran was sent down, as guidance for the people and as clear proofs of the guidance and the criterion.

**c2** (2:185): God says that He wants ease for them and does not want hardship for them.

**c3** (2:185): The verse gives as aims that they complete the period, that they magnify God for having guided them, and that they give thanks.

### One-minute summary

The Quran was sent down in the month of Ramadan, as guidance for the people and as clear proofs of the guidance and the criterion [c1]. God says that He wants ease for them and not hardship [c2].

### Complete story

The month of Ramadan is the one in which the Quran was sent down, as guidance for the people and as clear proofs of the guidance and the criterion [c1].

The verse says that God wants ease for them and does not want hardship for them [c2]. It gives as aims that they complete the period, that they magnify God for having guided them, and that they give thanks [c3].

### Deep study

This verse names the month in which the sending down took place [c1]. It describes the Quran by the words guidance, clear proofs of the guidance, and the criterion [c1]. It links the month to ease and to gratitude [c2][c3].

### Kids mode

The Quran was sent down in the month of Ramadan [c1]. It is guidance for the people [c1]. God says that He wants ease for us and not hardship [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the verse joins the sending down of the Quran to thanks for having been guided [c1][c3]. Another is that it states ease as God's wish [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the night of the month in which the sending down took place, or whether the sending down here is the same event as in the other chapters; the verse says only that the Quran was sent down in the month.
- Not established: whether 'sent down' here means all at once or in parts. Another story speaks of parts.
- The verse goes on to speak about fasting in this month and about those who are sick or travelling. Those provisions are not restated here; this draft gives no judgement on them, and a scholar should decide whether and how the page presents them.
- The Arabic word translated 'the criterion' (furqan) is read in more than one way and is left as a rendering for the reviewer.
